title: Who's spying on whom and why?
summary: NVIDIA's former CEO is alleged to have been compromised by a Chinese spy. We explore the state of spycraft in the contemporary age.

image.caption: In this image taken from video provided by TVBS, Alice Huang attends a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang, Nvidia's CEO, at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan, May 22, 2025. (TVBS via AP) ((TVBS via AP))

blocks.text: NVIDIA's former CEO is alleged to have been compromised by a Chinese spy. We explore the state of spycraft in the contemporary age.
Front Burner32:28Who's spying on whom and why?
The allegation that NVIDIA's former CEO is alleged to have been compromised by a Chinese spy raises all kinds of questions that sit at the heart of espionage and spycraft.
Since the time of antiquity, societies have sought to surveil and intercept communications both their friends and enemies.

Today, foreign intelligence services are working to cultivate relationships with politicians, penetrate businesses and universities, cultivate assets, steal valuable technology, and monitor dissidents living thousands of kilometres from home.

David Gioe is a former U.S. intelligence officer who now works as a visiting professor of intelligence and international security in the department of War Studies at Kings College London. He's our guest today.
